ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, senior officers and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List (for USD clearing and correspondent banking activity), and South Africa's domestic terrorist listings under POCDATARA. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in FIC Directive 6 receive enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth, source of funds, and independent verification of senior foreign political exposure. FATF high-risk jurisdiction screening is also required, and a negative media / adverse regulatory news search is completed for each UBO. Ongoing transaction monitoring and red-flag checks are maintained in accordance with the FIC Act guidance notes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All official name filings must be in South Africa's official languages in Latin script. If the intended name is in a non-Latin script, a romanized transliteration in English or Afrikaans must be provided. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, close corporation, trademark, or pending name reservation. The name must not falsely imply affiliation with any organ of state, university, professional body, or regulated financial institution. For a private company the suitability suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd' must be appended, and the full unrestricted name may not contain offensive or illegal expressions per section 11(2) and (3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: CIPC name reservations are valid for 180 days. No automatic online extension is available; if the company has not been incorporated before the reservation expires, a fresh CoR 9.1 application may be submitted after expiry, provided the name has not been taken. On rejection, the applicant may (i) submit an amended name list through the CIPC e-Services portal within 10 business days of the rejection notice, or (ii) file a formal application with the Companies Tribunal in terms of section 11(6) of the Companies Act and Companies Regulation 147 within 60 days of the notice of refusal. The Companies Tribunal application should state the grounds on which the proposed name complies with the Act and is not objectionable. A binding Tribunal decision is issued and, if set aside, CIPC must reserve the name and proceed with incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted by the CIPC for registered-office purposes only if a physical South African address, not being a post-office box, is disclosed and a registered agent's address is maintained. However, for a venture-capital general partner, the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) and major South African banks require a physical operational office and responsible persons available for inspection; a pure virtual arrangement without any physical presence will likely be rejected for FSCA licensing and bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% in the first three years, driven by FSCA licensing supervision, FIC accountability inspections, and SARS on-site audits, particularly because the entity will act as a financial-sector responsible institution and be subject to enhanced AML/CFT oversight.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 13-14, 19, 50, 66; Companies Regulations, 2011 (Regulations 9-11 and 24); Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002; Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - Business Registration Services
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1B)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; share consideration is subject to the solvency and liquidity test in section 4. No escrow account is statutorily required at incorporation. However, for the FSCA Category II Financial Services Provider licence, the applicant must evidence minimum capital of approximately ZAR 250,000 subject to the FSCA risk-based capital assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) via the bizCIPC e-Services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the bizCIPC e-Services platform and complete the CoR 9.4 name reservation application, entering up to three preferred names. Pay the prescribed online fee of ZAR 50 and await approval. A reserved name is valid for six months and must be substituted into the Memorandum of Incorporation before filing. If no name is reserved, the company may be incorporated with a registration-number name as provided in section 13(4)(a) of the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Completed CoR 9.4 name reservation form
Certified green barcoded ID or valid passport copy of each incorporator
Names, surnames, and ID numbers of proposed directors
Declaration of name availability preferences
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or undesirability, file a request for reconsideration through CIPC e-Services in terms of Regulation 9, or apply for a fresh alternative name. Where time is critical, proceed with incorporation under a registration-number name and reserve the preferred name subsequently.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - bizCIPC e-Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Digitally complete and execute the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and the standard Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1B) for a private company. Upload the documents on the bizCIPC portal together with the reserved name certificate. Pay the statutory fee of ZAR 175. Upon approval, the CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation and an enterprise registration number; the company acquires legal personality as of the registration date.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation
CoR 15.1B Memorandum of Incorporation (standard Pty Ltd form)
CoR 15.1A Incorporator's declaration
Certified ID/passport copies of incorporators and directors
Reserved name certificate (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the noted defects and resubmit the amended CoR 14.1 or MOI through the CIPC electronic correction facility. Alternatively, file a formal rectification application under section 91 of the Companies Act with a notice of non-compliance and supporting affidavit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Revenue Registrations with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company on SARS eFiling as an income taxpayer within 60 days of incorporation or commencement of business. Apply for VAT if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed ZAR 1 million; register for PAYE and UIF when employees are appointed. Obtain the Tax Compliance Status PIN required for contracting and FSP licensing. Income tax number and logistics of payment are established simultaneously with the corporate bank account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by CIPC
Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1B)
Directors' certified ID copies
Corporate bank account details (proof of account or letter)
Completed SARS registration forms (TRA, VAT101, EMP101 where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS will issue a notice of non-compliance or an additional information request; respond within 14 business days via eFiling with the required supporting documents. Where penalties have been imposed for late registration, file an application for remission or a formal objection under the Tax Administration Act, 2011, with a statement of just cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - Beneficial Ownership e-Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: In terms of section 50(3)(b) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 read with Regulation 24 (as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act, 2022), file the Beneficial Ownership Register with CIPC within 10 calendar days of incorporation. Identify each beneficial owner holding 50% plus one voting right, economic interest, or other significant control, and attach a declaration of significant control in the required format.
required_dossiers: Beneficial Ownership Register schedule (CIPC electronic BO form)
Certified ID/passport copies of each beneficial owner
Board resolution approving the beneficial ownership schedule
Shareholders' register confirming ultimate holding and control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC rejects the beneficial ownership declaration for incompleteness, correct the schedule and refile immediately. Any discrepancy regarding beneficial interest thresholds is cured by submitting a formal memorandum with the MOI and share register; further corrections are processed through the CIPC rectification procedure within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FSCA FAIS Category II Licensing for Venture Capital GP
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) jointly with the Prudential Authority of the South African Reserve Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Category II Financial Services Provider (FSP) licence under the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act, 2002. File the application digitally on the FSCA portal; evidence fit and proper requirements for directors and key individuals, risk-based capital, business plan with investor protection measures, and an effective AML/CFT compliance framework. Concurrently register the company as an accountable institution with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) and retain a designated compliance officer.
required_dossiers: FSP licence application (electronic FAIS 1 form)
Fit and Proper questionnaires for directors and key individuals
Business plan, operational infrastructure description and sworn statement
AML/CFT risk management and compliance programme under FICA section 42
Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
FIC registration confirmation as accountable institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSCA issues a request for information, respond within 30 calendar days. In the event of refusal, lodge a reconsideration with the FSCA or an appeal to the Financial Services Tribunal within 90 days of the decision. Interim corrections such as additional capital confirmation or replacement of non-compliant key individuals are accepted by way of supplementary filing without restarting the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality - Emergency Management Services and Department of Employment and Labour - Chief Inspector of Occupational Health and Safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm municipal zoning permits office-based financial services at the registered address. Obtain a Fire Safety Certificate following an inspection of the premises by the Emergency Management Services. Secure an Electrical Certificate of Compliance from a registered electrician and, where applicable, a structural load certificate. Comply with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 by conducting a risk assessment, appointing a health and safety representative, and obtaining a Certificate of Good Standing under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA).
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title deed for the registered office
Fire safety compliance certificate (EMS Form 2)
Electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC)
Occupational Health and Safety risk assessment report
COIDA registration certificate and Letter of Good Standing
Municipal planning approval or building plan consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire safety inspection identifies deficiencies, remedy the stated items and request a re-inspection. For COIDA late registration or non-compliance, file an application for late registration with the Department of Employment and Labour and pay any administrative penalty. Municipal zoning or building refusals are appealed to the Municipal Planning Tribunal within 21 days of the decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) and Prudential Authority (South African Reserve Bank), with the Financial Intelligence Centre for AML/CFT registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Category II Financial Services Provider (FSP) Licence under the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act, 2002

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based venture capital fund management does not constitute a listed activity under the EIA Regulations, 2014 (Listing Notices 1, 2 and 3); no Environmental Authorisation is required. Environmental due diligence is nevertheless advisable prior to funding PMI-level downstream industrial ventures of portfolio companies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater must discharge to the municipal sewer within by-law limits (pH 5.5-12.5; maximum COD 5,000 mg/l; suspended solids 1,000 mg/l). VOC and fuel emission thresholds are not triggered for administrative office use. Any waste generated, including e-waste, must be handled in accordance with the waste hierarchy and the National Norms and Standards for Disposal of Waste to Landfill (GN R 636) under the NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the municipal Emergency Management Services; Electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC); Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 risk assessment with compliance register; registration with the Compensation Fund (COIDA) and valid Letter of Good Standing; municipal zoning and building plan approval for the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); customs division handles export entries.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); register as a taxpayer on SARS eFiling; obtain an income tax reference number; appoint a SARS-accepted public officer resident in South Africa; submit VAT registration (VAT101) if taxable turnover exceeds the compulsory/voluntary threshold; obtain an export customs code from SARS Customs for export transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election. A South African (Pty) Ltd is an opaque, entity-level taxpayer. An eligible resident company may elect special headquarter-company treatment under section 9I of the Income Tax Act for certain foreign intra-group income; no hybrid mismatch or pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month rolling period; voluntary registration permitted once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in any 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time clearance, digital stamping, or fiscal storage control requirement is currently imposed. VAT tax invoices must contain prescribed particulars and be issued within 21 days of request/delivery/payment; SARS is piloting and has announced a future mandatory e-invoicing environment through eFiling/API, but it is not yet live.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for exported movable goods where the exporter holds documentary proof of physical export from South Africa to a foreign destination and satisfies SARS's export evidence requirements. The general partner's supplies of management services to non-resident funds may qualify as zero-rated exported services if the services are supplied to and consumed outside South Africa, subject to contractual and payment evidence.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS can disallow the zero-rating, assess output VAT, and recover refunds with statutory interest where export or service evidence is incomplete. Fraudulent or negligent export claims attract additional VAT under section 60 of the VAT Act, understatement penalties under the Tax Administration Act, and criminal sanctions for VAT fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, as administered via the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a current-account convertible regime with full transferability for bona fide trade, services, and profit repatriation, subject to documentary verification and tax clearance. Capital-account flows are administered via general allowances, institutional investment dispensations, or transaction-specific FinSurv approval. A licensed Venture Capital GP is an authorised institutional investor where funds are managed under an SARB/FSCA-approved institutional framework. Non-resident profits, dividends, and management fees may be remitted freely upon presentation of audited after-tax profit certification, SARS tax clearance (TCC), and (where applicable) dividends tax clearance. No exchange-control approval is required for routine operational remittances; capital calls from non-residents and outbound fund investments require Authorised Dealer reporting with correct BOP codes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory percentage conversion or surrender requirement applies. Export and invisible proceeds (e.g., management fees, carried interest) must be received in a South African Authorised Dealer bank account within 180 days of shipment/service completion or start of entitlement. Proceeds may be retained in foreign currency via a Foreign Currency Account, but all receipts must be reported under the relevant SARB BOP code and supported by invoices, agreements, and proof of the underlying transaction. No forced conversion to ZAR applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.sarb_finsur_approval_reference: Authorised Dealer general authority; FinSurv approval required for amounts above institutional thresholds or non-standard capital-account transactions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_flow_restriction_category: Institutional investor classification; per-transaction reporting above ZAR 10 million / institutionally approved limits; no restriction on non-resident beneficial ownership of the GP entity

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR account plus Foreign Currency Account (FCS)
Operational ZAR account plus Foreign Currency Account (FCS)
Operational ZAR account plus Foreign Currency Account (FCS)
Operational ZAR account plus Foreign Currency Account (FCS)
Escrow / capital-call collection account plus offshore-orientated trust and custody services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, subject to SARB National Payment System Act licensing / Prudential Authority authorisation. Offshore EMIs are not acceptable as the sole clearing rail for capital calls or subscription inflows because SARB exchange-control reporting requires all inward fund flows to be received through a South African Authorised Dealer. An offshore EMI may support ancillary payment processing, but the primary capital-call collection, ZAR settlement, and foreign-currency accounts must reside with a licensed domestic bank. FSCA/FIC Act AML obligations further disincentivize reliance on non-regulated foreign EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily absolute but is effectively required under FICA accountable-institution CDD policies. At least one director, signatory, or a duly appointed local authorised representative with power of attorney must attend a physical or video-linked onboarding interview (with geolocation and liveness verification). Most tier-1 banks require a South African resident director or local company secretary to enable full account opening if all directors are foreign. Certified/notarised corporate documents, apostilled memorandum of incorporation, and beneficial-ownership declarations are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership with multiple offshore LPs and intermediary holding layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FICA-compliant beneficial ownership register; full fund structure chart; natural-person identification for every >5% shareholder; notarised board resolutions; source-of-funds statements and underlying LP subscription agreements; legal opinion confirming the fund chain is not an unlawful concealment structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP flags on offshore investors or jurisdictions of domicile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU/UK/UN/SARB targeted sanctions screening results; PEP declarations with supporting source-of-wealth evidence; negative media reports; certified identity documents; legal opinion from a licensed South African attorney on sanctions exposure and connection to prohibited persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FSCA licensing uncertainty for the VC General Partner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FSCA FAIS/CSP licence or exemption letter; proof of the fund's registration as a private equity / venture capital fund; audited financials or solvency certificate; ISIC 6499 scope substantiation; regulatory status confirmation letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-call inflows arriving in fragmented small amounts from multiple non-resident jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital call notices; LP subscription agreements and side letters; bank-verified source of funds per investor; AML onboarding files per LP; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; fund waterfall and capital-call schedule evidencing legitimate investment flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected tax evasion via carried-interest or management-fee outbound remittances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements and tax returns; management agreement and carried-interest waterfall; SARS tax compliance status; transfer-pricing documentation (where foreign related parties exist); exchange-control approval or Authorised Dealer filing for foreign receipts; DTA-based dividend tax exemption evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital calls from non-resident LPs must be sent by SWIFT MT103 to the GP's ZAR capital-call collection account held with a South African Authorised Dealer, referencing the applicable SARB BOP code (e.g., 4480 inward investment in fund units). The bank will record the inflow under the Balance of Payments reporting framework. Each inward remittance must be matched to the executed capital call notice and LP identity record. The SARB individual discretionary allowance cannot be used for corporate fund subscriptions; instead, the GP must rely on the institutional investment dispensation or obtain FinSurv pre-approval where required. For collections in USD/EUR/GBP, the funds may be held in a fully-supported Foreign Currency Account without conversion, or converted to ZAR via the applicable spot rate upon documented instruction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements to fund SPVs, portfolio companies, service providers, or co-investors are executed via SWIFT MT103 (with MT202 cover where interbank settlement is required) through the Authorised Dealer, using BOP codes for outward direct investment (e.g., 4600/4601) or services. Commercial LCs are rare in VC treasury but permissible for structured acquisition transactions; the South African bank can issue an irrevocable documentary credit in favour of the overseas seller, subject to standard due diligence and any applicable transfer-pricing and SARB approvals. All transfers must be supported by underlying agreements (investment agreements, share purchase agreements, invoices) and reported via the SARB STR system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forward contracts (ZAR vs USD/EUR/GBP) for transactional exposure from capital calls and distributions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in ZAR/foreign-currency pairs, restricted to hedging genuine exposures
Cross-currency swaps for long-term foreign-currency commitments
FX options (vanilla calls/puts) over ZAR and foreign currencies for hedging uncertain exit proceeds
ZAR interest-rate swaps and FRAs to hedge bridge-financing rate exposure
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.hedging_eligibility_restriction: All hedging instruments are permitted only for bona fide hedging of identified exposures and must be transacted through an Authorised Dealer/FSCA-licenced counterparty; speculative derivative use by an unlicenced VC GP is prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.clearing_system_note: ZAR leg settles via the SAMOS RTGS system (South African Multiple Option Settlement), and all cross-border wires are processed via SWIFT and reported to SARB FinSurv under the Currency and Exchanges Manual.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC late-filing compliance flag and late penalty per the prevailing CIPC fee tariff; failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger Section 82 administrative deregistration and loss of good-standing status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) together with audited or reviewed annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the company's financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative non-compliance penalties and interest under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; SARS may raise a default or estimated assessment and block the company's tax-compliance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Risk and Compliance Return (ARCR) under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the date prescribed by FIC directive (commonly 30 April following the reporting period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative sanction of up to ZAR 10 million (approx. USD 550,000) per contravention under Section 87 of the FIC Act 38 of 2001; persistent non-filing heightens AML/CFT supervisory scrutiny.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FSCA levy payment and licence-condition annual financial statements for the licensed VC fund management entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the date published in the applicable FSCA levies directive; audited financial statements due within 4 months after the financial year-end where imposed as a licence condition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts interest; continued default may lead to suspension or withdrawal of the FSP licence and referral of directors to FSCA enforcement proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where (i) the company is a public or state-owned company; (ii) the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more at financial year-end under Companies Regulation 26; (iii) the controlling group prepares consolidated IFRS financial statements that include the Pty Ltd; or (iv) the MOI, shareholders' agreement, or FSCA licence condition requires an audit. A licensed VC GP/FSP is ordinarily required by FSCA licence condition to submit audited annual financial statements; otherwise, a private company with PIS below 350 may file independently reviewed AFS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and prescribed by Section 29 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; eligible non-public companies may apply IFRS for SMEs under Companies Regulation 27. Full IFRS applies where group consolidation, PIS, or FSCA conditions require. AFS must be approved by the board and presented to shareholders within 6 months after financial year-end.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Directors must confirm in the annual return that the Beneficial Ownership (BO) register is complete and accurate. Any allotment or transfer creating a new beneficial owner must be filed with CIPC within 7 business days under Section 50 and Regulation 23A of the Companies Act 2008, as amended by the General Laws AML/CFT Amendment Act. For a VC GP, investor transfers and capital-call share movements must therefore be reconciled before the annual-return deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders and share transfers)
Register of Directors (personal particulars, appointments and resignations)
Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO data and ID/tax reference numbers)
Register of Company Secretary (if such an officer is appointed)
Minute Book (board, shareholder and committee resolutions)
Annual Financial Statements and underlying accounting records (retained for 7 years)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 10,000 for a statutory audit; USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 for an independent review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday or preferential rate for a Proprietary Limited company acting as a venture capital general partner. The investor-side venture capital company incentive under s12J provides a tax deduction to qualifying investors, not to the GP manager. Reduced effective taxation may arise from deductible management-related expenses, assessed loss set-offs, and exempt dividend income received from South African companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to continuity-of-trade and change-of-ownership rules in s103(2) of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Company Income Tax Return; mandatory filing via SARS eFiling system (sars.gov.za)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (per financial year; provisional tax payments are made during the year as advance payments against the annual liability)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be submitted within 12 months after the company’s financial year-end. Provisional tax instalments are due within 6 months after the start of the year of assessment and at the end of the year of assessment, with an optional top-up payment due within 7 months after the year-end (for companies).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross annual receipts from management fees, carried interest allocations, and any other operating income derived from acting as general partner of an early-stage technology venture fund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a South African company owned by non-residents, report all worldwide gross income. Foreign-source income is subject to normal tax; double tax relief may be claimed as a foreign tax credit on a separate schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unutilised assessed loss from prior years available to be set off against current year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the loss arose from the same trade, and that no s103(2) change in ownership or trading continuity event has occurred; otherwise the loss may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17 – Taxable Income or Assessed Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable amount after deducting all allowable business expenses, capital allowances, and subtracting any assessed loss carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed under ordinary South African rules. Exempt dividend income (e.g., dividends received from South African resident companies) must be excluded from gross income and separately disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 27% of taxable income, before rebates and credits, reduced by the annual corporate rebate if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The rate is the same for resident and non-resident-owned South African companies. No additional branch remittance tax applies to a South African incorporated (Pty) Ltd.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit against South African normal tax for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income that is included in South African taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A schedule of foreign tax credits and supporting SARS assessment or tax official certificate is required; if no DTA exists, unilateral foreign tax credit relief applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the ITR14 triggers an administrative non-compliance penalty under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, ranging from R250 per month for small entities to R10,000 per month for high-turnover companies (capped at a fixed maximum in each category), plus a percentage penalty of 10% on any late payment of assessed tax, and interest at the prescribed rate (currently between 8.5% and 10.75% per annum, compounded daily).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% dividends tax imposed on the beneficial owner of a dividend paid by a South African company; the paying company (or transfer agent) must withhold and pay SARS.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce the 20% dividends tax below the statutory rate under a double tax agreement, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the paying South African company a SARS-recognised declaration (typically form DTD (Dividend Tax Declaration), sometimes called NRD) accompanied by a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the non-resident’s tax authority. The paying company must retain the declaration and TRC and file the dividend tax return (DTR01) with SARS, confirming the reduced rate (often 5% for a 10%+ shareholding, 15% for portfolio holdings). Reduced treaty rates will not apply retroactively if the declaration was not received before the dividend is paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to a non-resident: statutory withholding tax rate 15%, subject to exemptions for listed debt, government debt, and certain interest from banks and insurers. Royalties paid to a non-resident for IP or technical know-how: statutory withholding tax rate 15%. Under South Africa’s DTAs, the interest rate may be reduced to 0-10% and royalty rate to 0-10% (e.g., 0% under the DTA with the Netherlands for qualifying royalties; 5% under the DTA with the USA for certain interest and royalties). To claim any reduced rate, the non-resident must file an NRD form (Notice of Reduced Withholding Rate) with SARS and submit a TRC to the SA payer.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed monetary threshold is set in the South African Income Tax Act. Section 31 of the Act applies to any transaction between connected persons that affects actual or future taxable income. In practice, SARS expects contemporaneous Local File/Master File documentation and an arm’s-length benchmark for every material connected-party cross-border transaction; internal administrative guidelines often trigger detailed TP review where annual connected-party turnover exceeds ZAR 10 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no codified Economic Substance Regulation equivalent to UAE or BVI; however, common-law substance-over-form principles, the general anti-avoidance rules in s80A-L of the Income Tax Act, and s103(1) are applicable. Further, OECD BEPS Action 6 and the principal purpose test are applied in DTA claims. The GP entity should maintain a physical office, substantive decision-making powers, a majority of local directors, and actual performance of management and investment-decision functions; otherwise SARS may disregard the entity, recharacterise transactions, and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting management fee income, understating carried interest revenue, or creating fictitious expense vouchers and side agreements to reduce taxable income of the (Pty) Ltd.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upon an audit, SARS may impose an additional tax of up to 200% of the tax shortfall under s223 of the Tax Administration Act; criminal prosecution under s235 may lead to a fine of up to R10 million and/or imprisonment for up to 10 years, plus interest and cost of recovery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in tax evasion are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt and additional penalties. They may face criminal imprisonment (up to 10 years), travel bans under s250 TAA, and civil damages claims from minority investors. SARS may also apply a civil fraud claim.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the GP entity as a paper company with no real staff, no local board meetings, and no substantive management of the venture fund; channelling carried interest through an offshore related entity in a zero-tax jurisdiction while claiming treaty benefits on a conduit basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may disregard the transaction under the s80A-L general anti-avoidance rules and adjust the taxable income as if the arrangement had not been entered into; understatement penalties of 100%-150% for negligent or grossly negligent conduct; denial of DTA benefits under the principal purpose test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for the additional assessment and penalties. A court may issue a delinquency order under s162 of the Companies Act 2008, disqualifying them from serving as directors for up to 10 years, and order civil restitution of any profits improperly routed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register the GP entity with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC), failing to appoint a Money Laundering Compliance Officer and implement a Risk Management and Compliance Programme (RMCP), or failing to report suspicious transactions to the FIC; also failing to file beneficial ownership returns for the fund or the GP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 can reach up to R50 million for repeated serious non-compliance; criminal conviction for certain intentional contraventions may carry fines up to R10 million and/or imprisonment for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allow a failure to comply are personally liable to criminal prosecution, with a maximum fine of R10 million and/or imprisonment for 10 years. FIC Act s58A also authorises a court to order the director to pay restitution or be banned from holding any position of influence in a financial institution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging an excessive carried interest or management fee to a connected investee fund or a related offshore manager without performing a bench-marking study, or misallocating intangible asset rights to a shell entity to shift South African profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS will make a primary transfer pricing adjustment under s31 of the Income Tax Act, increasing taxable income by the under-declared amount; if the taxpayer fails to maintain contemporaneous documentation, an understatement penalty of 150% may apply; all additional tax bears interest at the prescribed rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or directed the transfer pricing policy are jointly and severally liable for the understatement penalty if the conduct is attributable to fraud or gross negligence; they may also be subject to a civil action for recovery of company funds and disqualification from the board of any company under the Companies Act.
